Curriculum: Early Years

We have high quality, motivated staff working together to provide a flexible, challenging and broad knowledge and skills-based curriculum, and a wide range of extra-curricular opportunities, delivered through a variety of activities both within and outside the school.
To this end, we have planned a curriculum which will engender curiosity, creativity and challenge.

They are: Within our positive learning culture, we strive to equip our children for today’s modern ever-changing world, to meet and overcome any challenges they may face so that they can become happy, healthy, well-balanced young people ready for their next stage in education.

Resource Base coming to Botley in September
In the Spring Term we ran a parent consultation on the opening of a Resource Base for pupils with high level autistic spectrum or communication and interaction needs. 100% of the responses were in favour of the plan, and we have been working with the DfE and the Local Authority to make the plan a reality.
The school received approval from the DfE for a change of status and the Local Authority have agreed funding for a Resource Base to open for some pupils in September of this year. When fully open, the resource base will cater for up to 16 pupils with high level needs across two classes.
In September, the plan is to open the first class for up to 8 pupils while we have some premises work completed in the school. We will then open the second class once the work has been completed. This is an extremely exciting opportunity for Botley and the wider community, so we are thrilled that we have received the go-ahead. We will keep people updated on this development over the coming weeks and months.

Special Educational Needs & Disabilities (SEND)
Supporting Every Child
At Botley School, we are committed to providing an inclusive education where every child can thrive. We believe that with the right support, every pupil can achieve their full potential.
Who to Contact
If you have questions about your child's progress or our SEND provision, please do not hesitate to get in touch by using the direct email or query form at the bottom of the page.
SEND Coordinator (SENCO): Miss Elspeth Doran
Email: botleysenco@botley.oxon.sch.uk
Our Provision & Approach
We offer a range of support tailored to individual needs, from "Quality First Teaching" in every classroom to specialised intervention.
The Enhanced Pathway: We are proud to offer a tailored curriculum for pupils with specific communication and interaction needs. This pathway uses a play-based learning philosophy based on the 'Engagement Model' (Exploration, Realisation, Anticipation, Persistence, and Initiation). It allows pupils to benefit from specialised support while remaining integrated with the main school community.
Graduated Approach: We follow the "Assess, Plan, Do, Review" cycle to identify needs early and put the right support in place.
Interventions: We provide targeted interventions for English, Maths, and social-emotional development (ELSA) for pupils who need a boost in specific areas.

Curriculum
At Botley School we foster engagement with learning and make the curriculum as rich and broad as possible. To this end, we have planned a curriculum which will engender curiosity, creativity and challenge. All the statutory requirements of the National Curriculum and the Agreed syllabus for Religious Education are met through our planning. The curriculum is organised in Key Stages. Key Stage 1 (ages 5-7 in Years 1 and 2) and Key Stage 2 (ages 7-11 in Years 3-6).
The Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum is followed by children in the Nursery and Reception classes. The organisation of curriculum content in each term has been chosen to provide cross curricular links which will enable pupils to embed knowledge. A greater depth of knowledge is further enhanced with the use of 'Curriculum Concept' questions which are included alongside the curriculum.
Learning behaviours and resilience are promoted through the PSHE curriculum and Growth Mindset skills that will help prepare our pupils for their next steps in learning and for life in the modern world.
The curriculum is delivered using a variety of teaching methods, sometimes whole class, sometimes group and sometimes individual.
The school has internal procedures for monitoring the curriculum. These involve the Headteacher, Senior Leadership Team and Curriculum Action Teams made up of teachers in school. Key subjects also have a named teacher as the subject lead.

Welcome to Nursery at Botley!
This page will give you lots of information about applying for a Nursery place and what happens afterwards. We hope you find it useful.
Children usually start Nursery the term after their third birthday. At Botley School we offer the 15-hour and 30-hour entitlements as well as offering you the opportunity to pay for additional sessions. These sessions will need to be requested the term before you wish to use them, and it will be allocated on a first come first served basis. Your sessions will be booked for the whole academic year unless you give us notice (one term) to alter it. Please note we are unable to offer ad-hoc additional sessions.

Admissions Arrangements
In the academic year your child turns 4, you will need to apply for a Reception school place through Oxfordshire County Council (OCC). The application process is open from the beginning of November until 15th January and you will be notified of the school place in mid April. Applications outside of this period would be considered as late applications. Please take a look at the OCC website for key dates, further information and the application form. If you are moving schools, you will still need to apply through the OCC website.
Transition into Reception
Once your child has been offered a Reception place by OCC, you will receive a welcome letter outlining the summer term events and an induction pack. The induction pack contains information about Botley School and Reception, including details about the school day, uniform, etc. You will also receive details about your child’s class teacher and a date for a one-to-one meeting.
During the summer term, we will contact your child's current Nursery/Pre-School, if they attend one, and arrange visits to meet your child in their current setting. We will invite you and your child to our transition morning and come and play sessions, where your child can spend time in the Reception environment, meet the staff, and get to know the other children starting in their class.
